articles.title: They scoped the customer and forgot the customer's ledger — a High-severity cross-tenant BOLA in Open Food Network
articles.excerpt: TL;DR What: POST /api/v1/customer_account_transaction in Open Food Network authorized against the class, not the record. It took customer_id straight from the request body, so a manager of Enterprise…
articles.body: TL;DR What: POST /api/v1/customer_account_transaction in Open Food Network authorized against the class , not the record. It took customer_id straight from the request body, so a manager of Enterprise A could create transactions against Enterprise B's customers — and read the resulting balance back. Impact: Arbitrary credit/debit of another enterprise's customer ledger, plus disclosure of that customer's running balance. CWE-639 + CWE-862, CVSS 7.1 (High) , integrity High . The part I like: the parent Customer model was correctly scoped per enterprise. Only the child transaction wasn't. And a feature-flag removal in 5.7.1 quietly made the bug reachable on every instance. Fixed in: OFN 5.7.4 . Advisory GHSA-7cqp-qvh5-7x85 , published 28 July 2026, credited to me as reporter. CVE pending.

articles.body: Enterprise AI automation is not scaled simply by giving more employees access to a workflow platform. It requires a repeatable operating model for training, review, security, deployment, and measurement. A cited n8n case-study claim describes training 100 employees and putting 65 workflows into production within a month, but those specific figures and the associated podcast episode could not be corroborated through available official n8n materials or credible third-party coverage. The useful question for organizations is therefore not whether a workflow total sounds impressive, but what evidence demonstrates that automation has become safe, governed, and operationally valuable.

articles.body: Our Quarkus monorepo CI pipeline had plateaued at 9–11 minutes on GitHub Actions free-tier hosted runners. After a focused optimisation pass, it now completes in about 5 minutes 20 seconds , without self-hosted runners, larger GitHub runners, or paid caching products. The key discovery was that the remaining time was not in dependency downloads or Maven compilation. It was in duplicate Quarkus work : repeated augmentation, repeated application boots, and infrastructure startup that some test suites did not actually need. This post walks through the changes that produced the biggest gains, the ones that barely moved the needle, and the final workflow shape.

articles.title: MLX vs llama.cpp on Apple Silicon (2026): Run a Local LLM in 5 Minutes
articles.excerpt: If you have an M1/M2/M3/M4 Mac, you can run real LLMs entirely on-device — no API keys, no cloud bills, and no prompts leaving your machine. Two tools dominate on Apple Silicon: MLX (Apple's own ML fr…
articles.body: If you have an M1/M2/M3/M4 Mac, you can run real LLMs entirely on-device — no API keys, no cloud bills, and no prompts leaving your machine. Two tools dominate on Apple Silicon: MLX (Apple's own ML framework) and llama.cpp (the portable C++ engine). Here's how to get MLX running in five minutes, and when to pick which. Why run local on a Mac? Privacy: your prompts never leave the laptop. Cost: $0 per token after the hardware you already own. Offline: works on a plane, in a cabin, anywhere. 5-minute MLX quick start MLX ships as a Python package (Python 3.10+): pip install mlx-lm Pull a 4-bit quantized model and run it: mlx_lm.generate \ --model mlx-community/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-4bit \ --prompt "Write a haiku about Apple Silicon." A 3B model runs comfortably on 16 GB of RAM.

articles.body: I've been reading almost exclusively LitRPG books for years now. It's a genre that leans heavily into fantasy while appealing to the side of me that loves diving deep into the mechanics of a chunky RPG. Having characters that level up as the series goes on is the kind of simple, yet addictive story development that really just hits the spot for me. I just can't get enough. With Matt Dinniman's Dungeon Crawler Carl series bringing LitRPG to mainstream media in 2026, I feel it's my duty to point out that there are other good books out there with similar elements. If you're looking for another well-written story with very likable characters who grow in power, I highly recommend checking out Will Wight's Cradle series.

articles.excerpt: Netflix has reportedly chosen to shelve David Fincher’s American Squid Game spinoff series, according to sources close to the project.
articles.body: Netflix has reportedly chosen to shelve David Fincher’s American Squid Game spinoff series, according to sources close to the project. Reports of the spinoff first surfaced in 2024, and it’s been slow going ever since then. Dennis Kenny, creator of the 2013 British thriller series Utopia, was attached to write the script, with Fincher set to direct. However, nothing moved forward for months — at least, not publicly. Then, in November 2025, the show was listed on the Film and Television Industry Alliance website with the title ‘Squid Game: America.’ The site listed a shoot date for February 2026 in Los Angeles, but given this most recent information, it’s safe to say this is no longer the case.

articles.body: The 2021 remaster of Quake has gotten a new, 19-level campaign co-developed by MachineGames in honor of the FPS' 30th anniversary. At QuakeCon, id Software and MachineGames announced a free new campaign for the 2021 version of Quake. The new campaign is titled Dawn of the Machine and is available for Quake owners right now at no extra cost. Ranger is stuck in a time loop and must solve puzzles and fight new foes using new weapons (including an axe!) to survive. It includes a new soundtrack, new deathmatch maps, and achievements. id Software and MachineGames have also ensured there will be a high degree of replayability with these levels, noting that the narrative presentation of the time loop allows for players to tackle them to their hearts' content and make new discoveries.

articles.title: Resident Evil Meets Papers Please in a Wild New Xbox Game Pass Offering
articles.excerpt: Quarantine Zone combines the zombie-apocalypse vibes of The Last of Us with bureaucratic drudgery
articles.body: Gamers are typically afforded a certain level of privilege when it comes to the zombie apocalypse. We’re usually cast as the heroes of these stories, empowered to sneak past the terrifying shamblers or take them down with a well-aimed bullet. Quarantine Zone: The Last Check , developed by indie studio Brigada Games and published by Devolver Digital, offers no such pampering. Instead, you’re working at a checkpoint, inspecting jittery survivors for symptoms to determine whether they’re healthy enough to be evacuated. The game’s been out for several months on Steam , and it recently came to Xbox Game Pass . If you’re a fan of survival horror, this unique genre mash-up is absolutely worth checking out.

articles.title: 'One more step': NASA astronauts conduct 6.5-hour spacewalk to prep ISS for solar array upgrade
articles.excerpt: Jessica Meir and Anil Menon completed a 6.5-hour spacewalk to install solar array mounting hardware outside of the International Space Station on Thursday, Aug. 6, 2026.
articles.body: Two NASA astronauts installed the seventh and final set of mounting hardware for new sets of solar arrays during a successful 6.5-hour spacewalk outside of the International Space Station. Jessica Meir and Anil Menon on Thursday (Aug. 6), assembled the modification kit for one of the space station's eight power channels, which will allow for the future addition of a new ISS Rolll-Out Solar Array (iROSA). Since 2021, astronauts on prior spacewalks have deployed six of the iROSA assemblies, leaving now just two awaiting delivery to the station later this year. Like building a giant erector set, Meir and Menon worked to assemble and bolt together the triangular brackets on the 3B power channel, located on the far right, or starboard (S6) segment of the station's backbone truss.

articles.title: Rocket Lab launches Japanese Earth-observing satellite after 5-week delay (video, photos)
articles.excerpt: Rocket Lab launched its eighth mission for the Japanese Earth-imaging company iQPS on Thursday morning (Aug. 6), five weeks later than originally planned.
articles.body: A Japanese Earth-observing satellite got to orbit early this morning (Aug. 6), five weeks later than originally planned. The spacecraft — a radar satellite that will be operated by the Tokyo-based company iQPS — lifted off atop a Rocket Lab Electron vehicle from New Zealand today at 5:18 a.m. EDT (0918 GMT; 9:18 p.m. local time). It was a deferred round two for the mission: Rocket Lab originally tried to launch it on June 30 but aborted that attempt at the last second . The company has not yet revealed what caused that abort. A Rocket Lab Electron rocket launches "The Grain Goddess Provides" mission for the Japanese company iQPS from New Zealand on Aug. 6, 2026.
